steps.what: Document precision agriculture source facts and validate their identifiers and units
Maintain consolidated precision agriculture records from validated source packets
Check consolidated records and reconcile missing or inconsistent agricultural information

tasks.design: Configure native import profiles in the farm-data {OTHER} before custom integration. The technician validates source identity and metadata once, fixed mappings consolidate the records, and discrepancies remain human work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment, field and laboratory data arrive in different formats.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed import profiles can repeat known field and unit mappings.
tasks.still_hard: Incorrect field identity, calibration differences and missing provenance.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise that a plausible number belongs to a different field or season.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated record transfer, with source-quality responsibility retained.

reach.task: Validate field and laboratory record provenance
reach.learn: Coordinate systems, units and seasonal identifiers

evidence.claim: Native import profiles can consolidate validated agricultural records; the saving is an unmeasured scenario requiring duplicate transfer today.

assumptions: Boundary is recording and consolidating source information, excluding collection operations, sampling design and map interpretation allocated separately.

Equipment operator supplies dated machine exports with device, field, operation, value, unit and calibration reference; laboratory supplies sample identifier, result, unit, method and quality before s1. Technician captures field identifier, season, time, coordinate reference system, source version and correction history in s1's 40 hours. Missing identifiers or units block automatic transfer and are resolved manually in s3.
OTHER means farm-data record software. Native imports are tested before custom code. Existing sensor acquisition and automatic storage runtime receive no new saving.
Additional source-format maintenance is counted as other-role work. Any shared source validation is owned here once, not repeated as a saving in map tasks.
research_questions: Can native imports remove repeated transfers after source validation and discrepancy handling?

incremental.description: Maintain mappings and regression-check changed source formats
Maintain machine and laboratory export metadata

tasks.short: Develop defensible geospatial soil sampling plans

steps.what: Specify soil sampling objectives, field boundaries and practical constraints
Develop georeferenced soil sampling grids from the specified design
Review sampling sites for representativeness and field feasibility

tasks.design: Configure a native geospatial grid tool in mapping {OTHER} from the technician's sampling specification. The technician checks representation, exclusions and accessible locations before releasing the exact sampling plan; no model chooses the sampling objective.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated point placement and clipping take time after the design is settled.
tasks.enabler_now: Native geospatial operations can generate and label a grid deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a design that captures soil variation without systematic bias.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise sites that are numerically valid but unrepresentative or inaccessible.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated grid production, with sampling-design responsibility retained.

evidence.claim: Native geospatial grid, clipping and point-labelling operations can repeat a specified sampling design; the local saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary covers sampling plan production and review, excluding collecting samples and laboratory analysis.

Technician validates boundary geometry and records coordinate reference system, design type, spacing or density, origin rule, exclusions, target analytes, depth protocol and point-label convention in s1's 40 hours. Boundary source is the farm's existing field register verified by the technician there. Missing geometry or practical constraints cause manual design and correction within s3.
OTHER means geospatial mapping software. Native grid generation is tested before custom code; already automatic point generation earns no new saving.
s3 includes field-feasibility checks and plan correction; no physical sampling effort is reduced.
unknowns: Boundary quality and sampling design requirements
research_questions: Does parameterised grid generation remove repeated point placement after feasibility review?

already_counted.description: Review and correct point placement and sampling feasibility

incremental.description: Maintain design profiles and coordinate-system tests

approvals.approved_version: Exact sampling point set, coordinates, boundary version, depth protocol and exclusions; changes void approval

steps.what: Divide fields into georeferenced zones using soil and production-potential evidence

tasks.design: Keep agronomic zoning judgement with the technician using geospatial {OTHER}. Native zoning tools can calculate candidate boundaries, but choosing whether those boundaries represent soil and production potential remains contextual analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: A computed cluster need not represent a stable agronomic difference.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing zoning capability supports analysis without demonstrating removed interpretation time.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing durable differences from weather, management and sensor artefacts.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a tidy zone map is agronomically misleading.
tasks.altitude: The technician retains agronomic zoning responsibility.

evidence.claim: Farmmaps provides variable-rate zoning and fertilisation task maps; that does not establish reduced time for contextual zoning judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is interpreting and defining agronomic zones, excluding source-record maintenance and routine map-layer production allocated separately.
OTHER means geospatial agricultural analysis software. No new structured production-potential score or machine-approved agronomic zone is introduced.
Native zoning calculations remain available; existing software runtime earns no new labour-saving credit.
Zero incremental upkeep because no zoning workflow change is proposed. Machine application prescriptions are outside this task.
research_questions: Do proposed zones remain agronomically meaningful when tested against independent seasons or samples?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, upkeep=0, net=0. Contextual zoning judgement is retained; existing calculations are not new savings.

tasks.short: Create and interpret layered agricultural maps

steps.what: Select agricultural map layers and specify their comparison and presentation
Create and layer maps using the specified transformations and symbology
Analyze agricultural maps and verify spatial and seasonal interpretation

tasks.design: Configure reusable native map projects in geospatial {OTHER} before custom code. Fixed transformations and layer styles rerun the technician's chosen composition; the technician checks alignment, resolution and meaning before using the map for advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated layer assembly and styling take effort after the comparison is specified.
tasks.enabler_now: Native map project templates can repeat known layer operations without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Comparing data with different spatial support, dates and management context.
tasks.human_edge: Separate a spatial coincidence from a defensible agronomic interpretation.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated map assembly leaves more time to inspect the evidence behind apparent patterns.

evidence.claim: Native geospatial project templates can repeat layer assembly and styling; the proposed task saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is map composition and interpretation, excluding source validation owned by record maintenance and agronomic zone decisions owned by the zoning task.

The technician's record-maintenance process supplies checked layer files with field and season identifiers, coordinates, reference system, values, units and quality before s1. s1's 35 hours includes selecting layer versions, extent, target projection, resampling method, date window, display breaks and no-data treatment. Missing compatibility information blocks composition and returns to manual investigation in s3.
OTHER means geospatial mapping software. Native saved projects are tested before custom code. Existing automatic rendering receives no new saving; repeated manual assembly must exist today.
Outputs are analytical drafts and do not control machinery or prescribe input quantities.
research_questions: Do saved map projects reduce assembly effort after alignment and interpretation checks?

already_counted.description: Verify alignment and interpret maps; correct composition exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain map projects and test changed layer schemas and reference systems
